lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eΔo \u0026lt; P\u003c/: "Δo < P → high spin; Δo > P → low spin (d⁴–d⁷)."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e\u003cb\u003eCFSE = −:
"

CFSE = −0.4·n(t₂g) + 0.6·n(e_g) (in Δo). Go through d¹ → d¹⁰ with H₂O: d³ (−1.2) and d⁸ (−1.2) are very stable; d⁰, d⁵ (high spin) and d¹⁰ have CFSE = 0. It explains trends in ionic radii and hydration enthalpies.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon seis ligandos sob:
"

With six ligands on the axes, the e_g orbitals (d_z², d_x²−y²) point toward the ligands and rise in energy; the t₂g (d_xy, d_xz, d_yz) point between them and drop. The difference is Δo. By the barycenter: t₂g at −0.4 Δo and e_g at +0.6 Δo.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn un ion libre los c:
"

In a free ion the five 3d orbitals have the same energy. Four have four lobes (d_xy, d_xz, d_yz, d_x²−y²) and one has two lobes plus a ring (d_z²). The colors indicate the sign of the wavefunction (blue +, red −).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eI⁻ \u0026lt; Br⁻ \u00:
"

I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO: from weak-field to strong-field ligands. Here Cr³⁺ with different ligands: Δo grows and the absorbed wavelength decreases. (Approximate values, with the Jørgensen model Δo = f·g.)

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara d⁴–d⁷ en octaedr:
"

For d⁴–d⁷ in an octahedron: if Δo < P the electrons spread over all the orbitals (high spin); if Δo > P they fill the t₂g first (low spin). Fe²⁺ (d⁶): with H₂O high spin (4 unpaired electrons); with CN⁻ low spin (diamagnetic).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eTetraédrico: el patró:
"

Tetrahedral: the pattern is inverted (e below, t₂ above) and Δt = 4/9 Δo, always high spin. Square planar: d_x²−y² very high; with d⁸ and strong ligands (Ni²⁺ + CN⁻) the 8 electrons fill the four lower levels → diamagnetic.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUna transición d–d ab:
"

A d–d transition absorbs light of energy Δ (λ = 1/Δ). The complex looks the complementary color. Cr³⁺ with H₂O absorbs ≈ 575 nm (yellow-green) and looks violet; with NH₃ or en it absorbs at a shorter λ and the color changes. With d⁰ or d¹⁰ there are no d–d transitions: colorless (except for charge transfer).

"
